resources.string: Rated or measured power of the appliance or group of appliances.
Length of the period in days (30 for a month).
Price per kWh from your bill, including taxes if you want the final cost.
Calculates the energy an appliance uses over a period and what it costs at the given kWh price.
Average illuminance the task requires. The annex of RIC No. 10 gives reference values by room and activity.
Height between the luminaires and the working plane (usually 0.85 m above the floor).
Total luminous flux of each luminaire, from its datasheet.
Fraction of the flux that reaches the working plane; it depends on the luminaire, the room index and the reflectances. Take it from the manufacturer\'s tables.
Loss from ageing and dirt: 0.8 in clean rooms, 0.7 or less in dirty ones.
Calculates how many luminaires a room needs using the lumen method: Φ = E·S / (UF·MF).
Measured power factor of the installation.
Power factor you want to reach, for example the minimum your tariff requires to avoid a surcharge.
Voltage the capacitor bank is connected to.
Calculates the reactive power of capacitors needed to improve the power factor: Qc = P·(tan φ1 − tan φ2).
Active power of the loads that must keep running.
Margin over the load for growth and starting currents (usually 20 to 30 %).
How long the batteries must last without mains (UPS).
Nominal voltage of the UPS or inverter battery bank.
Efficiency of the conversion from the batteries to the load.
Usable fraction of the capacity: about 50 % for lead-acid and 80 to 90 % for lithium.
Sizes a UPS or generator set for the load to back up, and the battery capacity for the required backup time. Requirements for emergency systems are in RIC No. 08.
